note: Synthesizes the official release/nightly SpiderMonkey js-shell API probes against the unchanged current full-string stax benchmark surface. This is not benchmark evidence, emitted JIT IR, optimized-code evidence, or a runtime-limit conclusion.

requiredGlobals.name: TextDecoder
requiredGlobals.reason: Full-string rows materialize UTF-8 XML spans as JavaScript strings.

requiredGlobals.name: TextEncoder
requiredGlobals.reason: Current generated-fixture and harness paths encode XML strings into Uint8Array fixtures.

requiredGlobals.name: ReadableStream
requiredGlobals.reason: Browser-compatible source paths and unchanged harness checks expect Web Streams.

requiredGlobals.name: fetch
requiredGlobals.reason: Browser-compatible live source rows and unchanged harness checks expect fetch.

requiredGlobals.name: Uint8Array
requiredGlobals.reason: Neutral byte-batch parser input is Uint8Array-based.

requiredSurfaces.label: StreamReaderSync Iterable<Uint8Array[]> full-string rows
requiredSurfaces.contract: Primary same-contract StAX rows over synchronous byte batches.
requiredSurfaces.reason: Uint8Array carries parser input, TextDecoder materializes StAX strings, and TextEncoder is used by the current generated-fixture harness.

requiredSurfaces.label: createEventReaderFromAsyncByteBatches full-string rows
requiredSurfaces.contract: Async byte-batch public event rows without direct ReadableStream consumption.
requiredSurfaces.reason: The parser input is Uint8Array[] and public event-object materialization still depends on TextDecoder.

requiredSurfaces.label: EventReader ReadableStream<Uint8Array> full-string rows
requiredSurfaces.reason: The public EventReader constructor checks for a Web ReadableStream and materializes strings through the same decoder-backed event path.

requiredSurfaces.reason: The live browser source rows require fetch, Response.body ReadableStream support, byte input, and full string materialization.

findings.summary: The official release and nightly SpiderMonkey js-shells are executable and can read binary XML, but both lack required Web-compatible globals for the current full-string stax benchmark unchanged.
This gap is a host API surface fact, not a SpiderMonkey throughput limit or emitted-code proof.
evidence: Adding a polyfill or alternate decoder would create a different harness surface and must not be counted as the unchanged current StAX full-string benchmark.
A diagnostic-capable shell or Firefox build can still close the emitted IR/codegen obligation.
